pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 깊은 산 아래 작은 오두막에 나무꾼과 늙은 어머니가 살았어요. 나무꾼은 날마다 산에 올라 나무를 하고, 새끼줄로 나뭇짐을 꽁꽁 묶어 지고 내려왔지요. 마당에 들어서면 머릿수건을 풀어 이마의 땀을 쓱쓱 닦았답니다. "어머니, 오늘도 다녀왔습니다!"
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a little hut at the foot of a deep mountain, there lived a woodcutter and his old mother. Every day the woodcutter climbed the mountain to cut wood, tied his load up tight with straw rope, and carried it home on his back. When he stepped into the yard, he pulled off his head cloth and wiped the sweat from his forehead. "Mother, I'm home again today!"

pages.ko: 어느 가을날, 나무꾼은 여느 때보다 훨씬 깊은 산속까지 올라갔어요. 어머니 방을 따뜻하게 지필 땔감을 넉넉히 하고 싶었거든요. 낙엽이 바스락바스락, 솔가지가 우수수. 어느새 해가 뉘엿뉘엿 기울었답니다.
pages.t: One autumn day, the woodcutter climbed much deeper into the mountain than usual. He wanted plenty of firewood to keep his mother's room warm and cosy. The fallen leaves went crunch, crunch, and the pine branches rustled down. Before he knew it, the sun was sinking low.

pages.ko: 그때였어요. 우거진 덤불이 부스럭— 하더니, 어흥! 집채만 한 호랑이가 떡 하니 나타났지 뭐예요. 나무꾼은 다리가 후들후들, 손에 쥔 지게작대기가 툭 떨어졌어요. '이, 이제 어쩌지…'
pages.t: And then it happened. The thick bushes went rustle-rustle — and ROAR! A tiger as big as a house stood right there in front of him. The woodcutter's legs went wobble, wobble, and the prop stick for his carrying frame dropped out of his hand. 'Oh no… what do I do now?'

pages.ko: 그 순간 나무꾼의 머릿속에 번쩍 꾀가 떠올랐어요. 나무꾼은 땅에 넙죽 엎드려 큰절을 올렸지요. "형님! 형님! 우리 형님! 산에 사는 우리 형님! 이제야 뵙습니다!"
pages.t: Just then a clever idea flashed into the woodcutter's head. He threw himself flat on the ground and made a deep, deep bow. "Big brother! Big brother! My own big brother! My big brother who lives in the mountains! At last I have found you!"

pages.ko: 호랑이는 눈을 끔뻑끔뻑했어요. "혀, 형님? 내가?" 나무꾼은 시치미를 뚝 떼고 말했지요. "어머니께서 늘 말씀하셨어요. 옛날에 산으로 간 큰아들이 호랑이가 되었다고요. 형님이 바로 그분이시군요!"
pages.t: The tiger blinked and blinked. "B-big brother? Me?" The woodcutter kept a perfectly straight face. "My mother always told me so. Long ago, her eldest son went up into the mountains and became a tiger. So you must be him!"

pages.ko: 호랑이는 한참을 가만히 있었어요. 그러더니 커다란 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁 맺혔지요. "그럼… 우리 어머니가 아직 살아 계신단 말이냐?" 뚝, 눈물 한 방울이 낙엽 위에 떨어졌어요. 어흐흑, 커다란 몸이 들썩들썩했답니다.
pages.t: The tiger stood still for a long, long while. Then great big tears welled up in his great big eyes. "Then… you mean our mother is still alive?" Plop — one tear fell onto the leaves. Oh-hoo-hoo, and his huge body shook and shook.

pages.ko: 호랑이는 나무꾼을 산길 어귀까지 데려다주었어요. "동생아, 어머니를 잘 모셔라. 나는 산을 지키마." 나무꾼은 꾸벅 인사하고 부지런히 산을 내려왔지요. 다리는 아직도 후들후들했지만요!
pages.t: The tiger walked the woodcutter all the way down to the mouth of the mountain path. "Little brother, take good care of Mother. I will guard the mountain." The woodcutter bowed and hurried down the hill. His legs were still wobbling, though!

pages.ko: 이튿날 새벽, 마당에 나온 어머니가 깜짝 놀랐어요. 커다란 멧돼지 한 마리가 새끼줄에 꽁꽁 묶인 채 마당 한가운데 떡 놓여 있지 뭐예요! "아니, 이게 웬일이냐?" 눈 위에 찍힌 커다란 발자국은 산 쪽으로 나 있었답니다.
pages.t: Early the next morning, Mother came out into the yard and got a big surprise. A great big wild boar lay right in the middle of the yard, tied up tight with straw rope! "Well now, where on earth did this come from?" And the huge footprints in the snow led away toward the mountain.

pages.ko: 저녁이면 나무꾼은 신틀 앞에 앉아 짚신을 삼으며, 산에서 있었던 일을 하나도 빠짐없이 말씀드렸어요. "어머니, 사실은 제가 꾀를 냈어요." 어머니는 한참 듣더니 고개를 끄덕이셨지요. "그래도 우리를 지켜 주는 마음은 참말이구나. 그럼 그이는 이제 우리 식구다." 그날부터 나무꾼은 저녁마다 산을 향해 소리쳤어요. 어머니는 그 옆에서 가만히 고개를 끄덕이셨지요. "형님! 형님! 우리 형님! 산에 사는 우리 형님!"
pages.t: In the evenings the woodcutter sat at his shoe-weaving frame, making straw shoes, and told his mother everything that had happened on the mountain, right down to the very last bit. "Mother, the truth is, I played a trick on him." Mother listened for a long while, then nodded her head. "All the same, the heart that watches over us is real and true. So from now on, he is family." From that day on, every evening the woodcutter called out toward the mountain, and Mother stood beside him and quietly nodded. "Big brother! Big brother! My own big brother! My big brother who lives in the mountains!"

pages.ko: 그 뒤로도 호랑이는 밤마다 살금살금 산을 내려왔어요. 어느 날은 산나물이 소복한 다래끼, 어느 날은 알밤 한 무더기. 놓아 두고는 뒤도 안 돌아보고 슬금슬금 돌아갔지요. 달빛에 커다란 등이 어른어른했답니다.
pages.t: After that, the tiger came creeping down the mountain night after night. One night, a little woven basket heaped with mountain greens; another night, a whole pile of chestnuts. He set them down and slipped away without ever looking back. In the moonlight, his great big back shimmered as he went.

pages.ko: 하루는 어머니가 마당 끝까지 나와 어둠을 향해 허리를 굽혔어요. "고맙구나, 우리 큰아들아. 밥은 먹었니?" 싸리 담장 너머에서 커다란 두 눈이 반짝, 코가 씰룩. 호랑이는 그 자리에 오래오래 서 있었답니다.
pages.t: One day Mother came right out to the edge of the yard and bowed toward the darkness. "Thank you, my eldest son. Have you eaten?" Beyond the brushwood fence, two great big eyes glittered and a nose twitched. The tiger stood right there for a long, long time.

pages.ko: 세월이 흐르고 또 흘렀어요. 어느 봄날, 어머니는 먼 길을 떠나셨지요. 그날 밤 산에서는 길고 긴 울음소리가 들려왔어요. 어흐응— 어흐응— 온 산이 함께 우는 것 같았답니다.
pages.t: The years went by, and by, and by. One spring day, Mother set out on her long journey. That night, a long, long crying sound came down from the mountain. Ah-hoooo— ah-hoooo— as if the whole mountain were weeping with him.

pages.ko: 그 뒤로 마당에는 아무것도 놓이지 않았어요. 하지만 나무꾼이 산에 오를 때면, 저 멀리 산등성이에 커다란 뒷모습이 서 있곤 했지요. 나무꾼은 머릿수건을 벗어 힘껏 흔들었어요. "형님! 형님! 우리 형님! 산에 사는 우리 형님!" 꾀 하나로 만난 사이였지만, 마음을 나누니 진짜 형님이 되었답니다.
pages.t: After that, nothing was ever left in the yard again. But whenever the woodcutter climbed the mountain, a great big figure would be standing far off on the ridge. And the woodcutter would pull off his head cloth and wave it with all his might. "Big brother! Big brother! My own big brother! My big brother who lives in the mountains!" They had met because of one little trick — but once they shared their hearts, he truly became a big brother.
